ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within circle $O$ with a radius of $10\,\text{cm}$, $AB=16\,\text{cm}$, and $OC\perp$ chord $AB$ at point $C$, what is the length of $OC$ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Join OA, as shown in the figure,\\
$\because OC\perp AB$,\\
$\therefore AC=BC= \frac{1}{2}AB=8$,\\
In Rt$\triangle$ OAC, $OC=\sqrt{OA^{2}-AC^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-8^{2}}=\boxed{6}\ (\text{cm})$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a circle with O as the center; inside the circle near the lower part there is a horizontal chord AB, and point C is on chord AB; from the center O, draw line segment OC downward to chord AB, and there is a right-angle mark at C, indicating that OC is perpendicular to AB. Reasoning: The problem gives that the radius of the circle is 10 cm, so OA = 10 cm; chord AB = 16 cm. Because the perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects this chord, AC = BC = AB/2 = 8 cm. Connect OA, then triangle OAC is a right triangle, in which OA is the hypotenuse and AC = 8 cm. By the Pythagorean theorem, OC = sqrt(OA^2 - AC^2) = sqrt(10^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(100 - 64) = sqrt(36) = 6 cm.

From the text, take the radius as 10 cm and the chord length AB as 16 cm. Use the theorem that the perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so AC = 8 cm. Then draw or consider radius OA, forming right triangle OAC with hypotenuse OA = 10 and leg AC = 8. Apply the Pythagorean theorem to get OC = sqrt(10^2 - 8^2) = 6 cm.
